title: Review: Transcription; Gene mutations; Chromosome mutations and polyploidy; Sources of genetic variation in meiosis and fertilisation
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AQA A-level Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: GE07#t4 term and clue written for the game; GE06a#t4 term and clue written for the game; CD04#t2 term and clue written for the game; GE04b#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: CD04#N.13, GE04b#N.8, GE06a#N.11, GE06b#N.14, GE07#N.6a, CD04#N.6, GE06a#N.6a, CD04#N.4, GE06a#N.3, CD04#N.12a. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Chromatids
items.clue: Members of a pair that normally separate from each other in meiosis II.

items.label: Frameshift
items.clue: Regrouping of every downstream triplet, because reading is in threes with no gaps.

items.label: Independent assortment
items.clue: Random orientation of each homologous pair at metaphase I, whatever the other pairs do

items.label: Introns
items.clue: Sections removed from the transcript; 980 of 1608 bases in the human β-globin example.

questions.stem: A mutation in a hypothetical species of animal prevents crossing over during meiosis, but meiosis is otherwise normal. Compared with the gametes of a normal individual, which prediction about the gametes of an individual with this mutation is correct?

options.text: Every gamete would be genetically identical, since crossing over is the only source of genetic variation.
They would vary less but still differ, because homologous pairs still orient randomly at metaphase I.
They would vary just as much as before, since crossing over just swaps sister chromatid segments.
Each gamete would carry either the full maternal or the full paternal set of chromosomes.

questions.stem: Using the β-globin gene data, what percentage of the pre-mRNA is kept in the mature mRNA?

In the allele that causes sickle cell anaemia, the mRNA codon for amino acid 6 of the beta chain of haemoglobin is GUG instead of GAG. GAG codes for glutamic acid and GUG codes for valine. What is the effect of this mutation on the protein?

options.text: One amino acid out of more than a hundred is changed, too small a difference to alter the structure or function of haemoglobin.
The reading frame is shifted from this codon onward, so every amino acid after it in the beta chain is different.
The codon GUG is degenerate, so the ribosome can still insert glutamic acid and the haemoglobin produced is normal.
Valine replaces glutamic acid at one position, which alters haemoglobin enough for it to form fibres at low oxygen concentrations.

questions.stem: When a new insecticide was first used on a crop, it killed nearly all individuals of a hypothetical pest insect. After several years of use, most of the pest population was resistant. Which statement best explains how resistance became common?

options.text: The insecticide caused the mutations for resistance that the insects needed to survive its use.
Insects that survived a dose built up resistance in their bodies and passed it to their offspring.
Every insect in the population gradually became more resistant until the whole population was.
Insects that already had resistance alleles from a random mutation survived and reproduced more.

questions.stem: A child has Down syndrome. Both parents have 46 chromosomes in each of their body cells. Which statement about the origin of the condition in this child is correct?

options.text: A mutation in the zygote altered the base sequence of one gene on chromosome 21, so the child carries a faulty allele of that gene.
The extra chromosome 21 was produced at fertilisation, when the nuclei of a normal sperm and a normal egg fused and their chromosomes combined.
One parent produced a gamete with 24 chromosomes because chromosome 21 failed to separate in meiosis, so the zygote had 47 chromosomes.
One parent's meiosis gave a gamete two copies of chromosome 21, and every other gamete from that division had the normal number of 23.

questions.stem: Which statement describes crossing over during meiosis?

options.text: The two sister chromatids of one chromosome exchange their segments in prophase I.
At a chiasma, all four chromatids of a homologous pair exchange segments in prophase I.
Non-sister chromatids of a homologous pair exchange segments in prophase I.
Homologous pairs swap the sides of the plate they face at metaphase I.

questions.explanation: While homologues are paired in prophase I, non-sister chromatids exchange corresponding segments at chiasmata, making new combinations of alleles.

questions.stem: In mRNA the codons GCU, GCC, GCA and GCG all code for alanine. A base substitution in a gene changes the codon GCU in its mRNA to GCC. What is the effect on the polypeptide?

options.text: Alanine is replaced by a different amino acid at that one position
None: the same amino acid, alanine, is placed at that position
The reading frame shifts, changing all amino acids after it
Every amino acid in the polypeptide is changed to another one

questions.explanation: GCC codes for alanine just as GCU does. Because the code is degenerate, a base substitution may or may not change a single amino acid.

questions.stem: Garden peas have a diploid number of 14. Ignoring crossing over, how many different combinations of maternal and paternal chromosomes can random orientation of bivalents produce in the gametes?

options.text: 7 different combinations
14 different combinations
16 384 different combinations
128 different combinations

questions.explanation: 2n = 14 means 7 bivalents. Each can face either way, independently: 2⁷ = 128.

questions.stem: Part of the base sequence of a gene is GAT TCA GGC ATT before a mutation and GAT TCG GCA TT after it. Which type of gene mutation has occurred?

options.text: A substitution of the base A by G at the sixth position in the sequence
A chromosome mutation, because the total amount of DNA has changed
A deletion of one base, which has moved every later base one position along
A substitution that has shifted the reading frame of later codons

questions.explanation: The A in the second codon is missing and every base after it has moved up one place; the mutant is one base shorter. This is a deletion.

questions.stem: In one meiosis in a parent, the first division is normal. In the second division, the two chromatids of chromosome 21 fail to separate in one of the two cells; the other cell divides normally. How many chromosomes are in each of the four gametes from this meiosis?
questions.explanation: Only one of the two second divisions went wrong: it gives one gamete with an extra chromosome 21 (24) and one without it (22). The other cell gives two normal gametes.
